title: Juniors who hold substance-perishing; Chassanis; we prefer renovation yet dare not harshly reject
pass_a_gloss: Meanwhile we more approve the former sentence. For this reason we dare not reject harshly the sentence of those who judge that the world will perish according to substance — especially since nothing about it stood as defined of old by any synod, and certain truly outstanding men dissent about it. Psalm 72:7. Job 14:12; Luke 21:33; also Psalm 102:27–28; Revelation 20:14 and 21:1 seem to favor his sentence, where it stands as expressly said that the sea will stand as no more; Certain belonging toward the juniors dissent from all these, namely Johannes Chassanis, a French theologian (Common Places book 3, chapter 22).
pass_b_english: Certain of the juniors dissent from all these, namely Johannes Chassanis, a French theologian (Common Places book 3, chapter 22). Revelation 20:14 and 21:1 seem to favor his sentence, where it is expressly said that the sea will be no more; also Psalm 102:27–28; Luke 21:33; Job 14:12; Psalm 72:7. For this reason we dare not reject harshly the sentence of those who judge that the world will perish according to substance — especially since nothing about it was defined of old by any synod, and certain truly outstanding men dissent about it. Meanwhile we more approve the former sentence.
source_text: Dissentiumt ab omnibus istis quidam juniorum, nominatim Johannes Chassanis, Theologus Gallus, Loc. Com. lib. 3. cap. 22. Cui sententiae favere videtur Apoc. 20.14. & 21.1. ubi disertim dicitur, mare non fore amplius; Psal. 102.27.28. Luc. 21.33. Jobi 14.12. Psal. 72.7. Hacpropter neque horum sententiam praefracte rejicere audemus, qui mundum secundum substantiam periturum esse arbitrantur: praesertim cum nihil de eo antiquitus synodo ulla sit definitum & quidam praestantes sane viri de eo dissentiant. Interim priorem sententiam magis probamus.
